articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities in Latest Action
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026. This action is part of ongoing efforts to target networks supporting the Iranian regime and its illicit activities.
These designations fall under Operation Economic Outcast, which aims to disrupt financial channels used by Iran.
Further details on the specific entities and individuals designated are available on the Treasury Department's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Cyber-Related and Transnational Criminal Organization Designations, Targets Cuba
body: On November 5, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new Cuba-related sanctions.

The Cuba designations include a determination under Executive Order 14404, authorizing sanctions against foreign persons operating in Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors.
The State Department also designated eight entities and two individuals, and identified five vessels, for supporting Cuba's oil shipping networks, state-owned entities, and military supply chains.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran Designations, Alert on False Flags, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, as part of Operation Economic Outcast.
OFAC also issued an alert highlighting the substantial risk of designation or penalties for providing services to vessels using false flags to evade U.S. sanctions on Iran.

Additionally, an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL 5AA) was issued, authorizing certain transactions involving the PDVSA 2020 8.5% bond on or after December 18, 2026, replacing General License 5Z.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-Related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License. This amendment aims to clarify or adjust existing authorizations related to transactions involving Iran.
The specific details of the amendments are available on the Treasury Department's website, and stakeholders are advised to review the updated guidance for compliance purposes.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Linked to North Korea and DRC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities and individuals related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
The North Korea designations address government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes that allegedly defraud U.S. companies and generate revenue for North Korea's weapons programs.
The DRC-related designations target individuals and entities accused of supporting armed groups in the region.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.

These updates aim to provide clearer guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC's regulations. The amendments are intended to streamline reporting processes and enhance understanding of OFAC's requirements.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran, Russia GLs; Removes Belarus, North Korea Designations
body: On October 21, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea.

Additionally, OFAC issued new general licenses for Iran and Russia, and amended existing Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance on these changes. These actions reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Under PAIPA, Issues Associated General Licenses
body: On October 19, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA).
These designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated general licenses, which aim to mitigate unintended consequences and provide specific authorizations for certain transactions.
The PAIPA designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating intellectual property theft and protecting American innovation.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question on October 16, 2026.
These updates provide further clarification and adjustments to existing authorizations concerning transactions involving Venezuela.
Stakeholders are encouraged to review the updated guidance to ensure ongoing compliance with U.S. sanctions programs.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Pays $1,529,685 to Settle OFAC Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle its potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.
The violations involved exports from the United States to JSC Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian missile manufacturer, between September 2018 and March 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed but egregious, stemming from insufficient due diligence after Extreme's Russian subsidiary acquired customer accounts and contracts, including one naming MMZA as an end user.

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.
This deregulatory action aligns export controls on suppressors with the controls already applied to firearms, aiming to alleviate compliance burdens while protecting national security.

Under this new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), and a license will be required for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, with existing license exceptions for firearms also applicable to suppressors.

articles.headline: Extension of the Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
